name: Guildford
description:
Guildford cut its teeth keeping secrets.

In days when magic was outlawed, you would have taken it for a perfectly mundane city. But say the right word to a baker or wink just so at a greengrocer and they would take you through a hidden doorway and into the real city: a veritable hive of sword and sorcery. Hundreds of secret factions permeated the city: conjurers, abjurers, acolytes of newfound deities, wielders of enchanted steel - all diligently exploring, forging new arcane traditions behind false walls and under rug-covered trapdoors.

Those days are long gone and magic is now as everyday as mealtime, but the factions - now legitimate, openly-operating Guilds - retain their old fronts: the Thieves' Guild's tower has a bank at its base, the Congress of Independent Rangers meets in a converted stables, the Third Wizards' Guild is accessed through a pastry shop. Indeed, the guilds of Guildford are so numerous that practically every mundane business cohabitates with one or more of them, though many are humble and exasperating in their pedantic specificity: "The Ninth New Reformed Paladin's Guild," etc. As you might imagine, the order of the day is fierce competition between all these Guilds. As magic traditions diverge, merge and re-branch, power shifts, Guilds rise and fall, and of course there are the bridges.

Nobody remembers which Guild built the first bridge across the wide, shallow course of the River Fleet, but many others followed, until the river was barely visible among the innumerable spans, each uniquely adorned and constructed from increasingly unusual materials. These days, if a Guild has a poor reputation, it is said that they "do not have a bridge." These bridges, representing pride, status, and significant capital investment, now serve as meeting places and venues for public display of new arcane achievements.

But even as the Guilds bring their magical traditions into the light of day, their tightening grip on the city breeds discontent, and while they busy themselves with their bridge-building, others construct new hidden chambers and secret doors...

Which guilds will rise and which will fall? Who will benefit? Who will rebel? What secrets does the city now keep?

hooks.name: The Museum of Obsolescence
hooks.description:
A visit to the Musem of Obsolescence will acquaint you with its strange caretaker, the kind and terrifying Modthry, a rust-faced creature whose humanoid torso terminates in a confusion of wooden, vine-like legs, and whose elderly affect hides a fearful strength.

He is cheerful, if sleepy, and will happily guide visitors through his museum, which is filled with innumerable cast-off artifacts from the Guilds' rapid phases of arcane advancement. Such a dusty, forgotten corner of the city would hardly seem worth notice, but Modthry will tell you that he is plagued by near-constant burglary attempts.

What does Modthry have in his collection that is so desirable? Who is after it?
hooks.gmNotes:
Multiple Guilds are after multiple objects the museum. The objects' nature, the Guilds' purposes, and their methods of burglary are entirely up to you.

You can use Modthry to nudge Our Heroes toward one side or the other of the exchange. A Modthry who expresses concern about the increasing sophistication of the burglary attempts may invite assistance. A Modthry who declares that he repulses all attempts handily and who is frustratingly fastidious about his collection may motivate the party to find and take up with one of the burgling Guilds. Or perhaps one of said Guilds comes to Our Heroes with an irresistible offer for their aid in their next burglary attempt.

However you set it up, the important thing is that Our Heroes are present in the museum during a burglary attempt that goes well until three things happen at once: 1) It becomes apparent that multiple groups of burglars are burgling at the same time; 2) Some spell or artifact causes all the objects in the museum to come to life and attack anyone and everyone within reach; 3) Modthry is revealed in his full, terrifying strength.

(Bonus points for having your players contribute ideas for obsolete objects that might be in the museum ahead of time, so they must then battle their own creations.)

If one or more of the burglaries should succeed (and if it is a burglary Our Heroes were assisting with, perhaps their associates turn on them, leaving them at the mercy of the animated objects and Modthry's wrath) consider a subsequent quest to attempt to retrieve the object from that Guild's headquarters, which should of course be outfitted with all manner of defenses and obstacles appropriate to that guild.

hooks.name: A Night To Remember
hooks.description:
The Knights' Guild Arena is the grand stage of combat for the city. Here the pageant of chivalry is performed in all its stuffy, bloody glory by a rotating cast of local and traveling knights.

Attendance has been steadily falling, however, as the arcane arts have increasingly captured the attention of the city, and the Guildheads have stubbornly refused to add magic to the Arena bouts. Things have become desperate enough for them, apparently, that they are now willing to rent out the Arena to other Guilds, and it's one such rentals that has the city buzzing.

An open call for combatants has gone out, with great rewards promised, but few details offered. The arena has been strictly off-limits, but high scaffolding has been visible above its rim, and a there's a rumor that one of the Wizards' Guilds specializing in illusion magic has been contracted for the event.
hooks.gmNotes:
It's up to you whether the Guild putting on this event makes themselves known to the public or remains mysterious. Whoever they are, they should have ambitions of power, and it is their goal to gather together as much of the city as possible, then spring their trap.

Our heroes may be participants or spectators, but either way, the event should have every appearance of a no-expense-spared production: full-scale realistic scenery, actors and beasts real and illusory, narrative, drama, comedy, tragedy - the point is that everyone is drawn into the show and forgets about the strange circumstances of its staging.

And that's when the show starts to get too real. Stage combat becomes real combat. Actors in monster costumes are replaced by real monsters, spike pits have real spikes at their bottoms, spells that were for show before are dealing damage now. Maybe some of the conflict spills out into the audience.

In the midst of this chaos, the show should go on: the narrative must continue on toward its climax, the crowd must still be eating it up. And it is the climax where the real intentions of the evening's hosts are revealed. These are up to you: a ritual summoning an evil deity, the assassination of a prominent Guildhead, a permanent takeover of the arena itself, etc.

Bonus points for giving each attendee some sort of souvenir object that ends up aiding the ritual in some way (commemorative coins, perhaps?). If the secret host Guild has some knowledge of and/or grudge against Our Heroes, further bonus points for making the narrative of the show a parody of the party's adventures to-date, adding insult to injury.

hooks.name: Battle On The Bridges
hooks.description:
The First Wizards' Guild and the Second Wizards' Guild have never gotten along. More than once their leadership have nearly come to blows at city council meetings. When one built a bridge, the other built a grander one right next to it.

Now, after yet another public row, the Guilds have challenged one another to settle their differences once and for all with a battle - to the death - to take place upon their neighboring bridges in three days' time.

The city council is deeply concerned, as the arcane prowess of these guilds is as renowned as their wrathfulness, and they fear the battle may expand to engulf the city. They are offering a handsome reward for anyone who can broker peace between the guilds, as well as generous wages to any brave enough to stand guard on the edges of the battle, should it take place.
hooks.gmNotes:
The precise nature of the two Guilds is up to you, but consider differentiating them significantly: have them each specialize in a specific school of magic, give them diametrically-opposed theories on the origins of magic, etc.

If Our Heroes choose to pursue the diplomacy route, this is an opportunity to give them some information about both the personalities at play and the strategies each side is likely to employ in battle. If it's interesting to you to give them a path to resolving the situation, that's of course a possibility, but most likely, this is all a preamble to the fun part, which is of course a big, wild wizard battle.

The bridges should be very different, should be close enough to be within the range of most spells, and should themselves play a role in the battle. Perhaps one bridge amplifies damage while the other reduces it, or one has pods that transmute combatants into beasts while the other flings its own bricks at foes.

However you set it up, it should be large in scale, chaotic in nature, and should escalate quickly. Perhaps other Guilds' bridges also become part of the battlefield - or even the river below. It should feel big and out of control, but Our Heroes should have some insight into each of the Guilds that allows them to diffuse the bomb even as it's going off.
